correctness.rationale: The frozen RESULT.md reduces the convex hull support function to W(t)=max(2R sqrt(1-t^2),(R+r)sqrt(1-t^2)+Ht), t=|u_z| uniformly on [0,1]. Inverse quadratic roots plus the unsquared condition w>=H on the upper root justify all survival branches. Differentiation and endpoint comparison independently give H1^2=R^2-r^2, H2^2=(R-r)(3R+r), H3^2=(R+r)(3R-r), with H3^2-H2^2=4Rr>0. Integration yields the stated mean. My independent numerical quadrature checks 240 CDF cases, not all heights; the continuous argument proves the universal claim. The limiting cone r=0 and cylinder r=R do not have three distinct thresholds.

value.rationale: An exact probability distribution rather than only mean for a familiar 3D solid is a natural intrinsic geometry invariant. The separation of three local/global extremal transitions for genuine positive unequal radii, and square-root onset of the fraction of directions wider than 2R, are nontrivial structural boundary statements relevant to shape stereology and testing projected-width models; these cannot be obtained by citing an average or the cone endpoint.
